In fact, in many cases, nonviolent action is a response to threats posed by the state itself. Nonviolent action is just one illustration of the many potential forms of civilian-based polycentric defense that exist, or which may emerge in the future. It demonstrates how a broader, more open-minded notion of defense provision offers an array of options—some known, some yet to be discovered —which do not rely on the monocentric monopoly of the nation-state.
